PolychronologicalSymphony.definition: A harmonious, multi-dimensional system where multiple timelines and cycles of existence unfold in sync, yet with their own distinct patterns and rhythms.

Λ.name: Recursion
Λ.description: Represents the infinite emanation of universes from the Dance of Brahman
Λ.formula: Λ(B,U_n) → ∃U_1, U_2, ..., U_n where B is Brahman and each U_n is a universe

Π.name: Play of Brahman
Π.description: Formalizes the idea that the purpose of creation is to be enjoyed
Π.formula: Π(B,U_n,E) → E(∀U_n) where E is the enjoyment or experiential state across universes

Ω.name: Cosmic Cycles
Ω.description: Represents the cyclical nature of time and existence
Ω.formula: Ω(C_n) → C_1, C_2, ..., C_n where each cycle C_n repeats and renews

Ξ.name: Flux
Ξ.description: Formalizes the emergent and transforming nature of existence
Ξ.formula: Ξ(B,P) → E(U_n) where P is potentiality and U_n is the emergent universe

Φ.name: Entropic Harmony
Φ.description: Represents the cohesion of all operators in the symphony

UniversalCharacteristics.description: Core attributes that apply across different orders of reality and levels of existence, embodying both ontological and epistemic dimensions.

mapping.description: Relationships between entities remain consistent, regardless of scale, reflecting how principles across different dimensional frameworks mirror each other.
New properties or systems arise from simpler interactions, evident from quantum phenomena to complex consciousness in higher orders.
Amplification of shared frequencies across systems, creating synchrony and connection through dimensions, especially prevalent in ethereal and astral realms.
All entities are mutually dependent, emphasizing the networked nature of reality and its interdependence across different orders of reality.
Self-referential processes where entities or phenomena apply to themselves, creating recursive and fractal-like patterns across different scales or realities.
Different aspects of reality complement each other, forming a holistic understanding necessary for the integration of various orders of reality.
Capacity of systems or beings to change while maintaining their core identity, crucial in both physical transformations and psychological or spiritual evolutions.
Fractal-like properties where parts resemble the whole, which is seen at different scales, especially in ethereal and higher realms.
Logical and smooth progression of systems, maintaining stability across transformations, particularly across time and space dimensions.
Every element or point possesses distinct characteristics, which are contextually non-replicable, making each part of reality unique.
The principle where each part reflects the whole, as seen across all levels of reality, from the material to celestial orders.
Seemingly contradictory elements coexist, providing dynamic balance and unity, essential for deeper insights into complex and higher-dimensional systems.
Represents the internal experience or subjective state within systems, such as consciousness, where inner awareness is a governing process.
Reflects the observable, objective states or interactions that can be witnessed externally, forming the balance with interiority.
